subject: Post-call: ZenithAI TCO & cost optimization (token economics, batching/caching)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@zenithai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ZenithAI TCO & cost optimization (token economics, batching/caching)

Hi Alex 1

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Monthly token spend volatility due to bursty autocomplete traffic (especially during marketing pushes).
- Current provider costs are ~ $45k/month and unit economics are unpredictable under load.
- Tight latency SLOs (95th <= 200ms) for user-facing features; caching currently limited to session-level caching.

Goals you outlined:
- Reduce monthly inference spend by 30-40% while keeping P95 latency <= 200ms.
- Implement predictable billing model for forecasting and exec sign-off.
- Run a pilot to validate batching/caching savings on your autocomplete workload.

Preliminary TCO levers we discussed:
- Token-level economics: moving to Redwood's streaming/batched inference reduces per-token compute by ~25% for short prompts (we'll model this against your request-size distribution).
- Intelligent batching: for your autocomplete traffic we estimate 2-3x improvement in GPU throughput during bursts with minimal latency impact when combined with smart strict-priority routing.
- Prefix/KV caching: reusing prefix KV cache for common prompts (search/autocomplete templates) can cut repeated token generation by ~15-20%.
- Quantization profile: evaluating 4-bit quantized variants for non-critical rerank steps to further reduce GPU cost.

Attachments I'm sending: a filled TCO model (zenithai_token_tco_model.xlsx) with conservative / base / aggressive scenarios and a preliminary pricing estimate (redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
1) Rafael and I will run the attached TCO model against your October logs - can you share a 7-14 day sample of request logs (anonymized is fine)?
2) Schedule a 30-min pilot planning call this week to define success metrics (cost per active user, P95 latency, errors) - I'm available Wed/Thu afternoon PT.
3) If the pilot math aligns, we'll propose a limited Dedicated pilot or hosted trial with reserved burst capacity and a short-term commit to secure pricing.

Open questions from my side:
- Do you have any regulatory constraints around logs retention or on-prem compute we should factor in?
- What's the internal budget window and timeline for a decision (e.g., finance approval needed by end of Q4)?

Thanks - I'll sync with Rafael and get the initial TCO scenarios over by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0132

--
Attachments: zenithai_token_tco_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf (PDF)

Thanks Marissa - really helpful summary. A few quick answers: 

- We can share a 14-day anonymized request log dump (will remove user_ids). I'll ask engineering to prep and should have it by EOD tomorrow.
- No on-prem requirement for the pilot; we prefer hosted but may evaluate Private for long-term compliance.
- Budget: our finance team is aiming for a Q4 decision with a target to reduce spend by at least 30%. Execs want to see conservative savings estimates.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you include a conservative case that assumes only 10-15% effective batching for autocomplete (we saw optimistic numbers in other vendors but want conservative realism)?
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood's billing can provide per-route cost breakdowns for the pilot so we can map savings back to product areas?

Also tagging Priya Rao (cc: priya.rao@zenithai.com) who'll be our procurement lead for any contract discussions.

Appreciate it - looking forward to the model.

Alex
